purpose: Expanded architecture for representing religion as a living historical tree embedded in a wider field. It complements religious-foundation-blueprint.json rather than replacing it.

entity.scope: Historical and contemporary religious formation, transmission and branching.

time.description: Multiple clocks rather than one founding date

questions: What field existed before the tradition emerged?
What neighboring traditions influenced or contested it?
religious_ecology.principle: The field does not disappear when the tradition is born. The tradition remains embedded in and changes the field.

comparative_method.prohibited_shortcut: Do not infer common historical origin from structural resemblance alone.

evidence_model.rule: Never collapse sacred timeline, historical reconstruction, material evidence and project symbolism into one factual layer.

validation_rules: foundation_id must resolve to a foundation record
branch relationships must preserve timeline where timeline is claimed
sacred timeline must not be presented as historical dating
later texts must not be treated as contemporaneous evidence without support
archaeology can attest material practice but not automatically theology
structural similarity is not proof of historical influence
modern institution must not be equated with the whole historical tradition

implementation_notes.canonical_owner: This blueprint governs the architecture of a tradition; foundation, person, text, place, institution and event records remain independent canonical nodes.
implementation_notes.frontend: Use tree/timeline views as secondary navigation. The detail page must expose substantive evidence and historical phases first.
known_traps: one founding date hides multiple historical clocks
later institutional labels can be projected backwards
modern revivals can be mistaken for continuity
comparative resemblance can be mistaken for borrowing
implementation_notes.research_task: For each major tradition, build the formation and transmission timeline before expanding symbolic or comparative graph edges.

quality_rules: Use ranges for uncertain ancient dates.
Keep sacred timeline separate from historical reconstruction.
Affiliation is not intensity of belief.
Historical tradition is not identical to modern institution.
A later text may preserve earlier tradition but is not automatically contemporaneous evidence.
Archaeology can attest practice or settlement but does not prove theological interpretation.
Project-symbolic claims must be explicitly marked as such.
